name: Procter & Gamble

header.one_liner: Staples compounder at its slowest: 1% organic growth, an 8% EPS cost drag guided for FY27, and a yield that loses to Treasuries.
header.thesis: FY26 core EPS rose 1% and FY27 guides to flat to +3%. At 22x against a 5.2% Treasury the engine's base case earns well below the hurdle.

rev_cagr.why: FY26 organic growth was 1% and FY27 guidance is 1% to 3%.

margin_end.why: Net margin is about 18.6% (core). FY27 carries about $1B of after-tax cost headwinds ($0.56 a share, an 8% drag), so the base case dips slightly.

share_chg.why: About $5B of buybacks planned in FY27 against a $364B market cap.

exit_pe.why: Currently 22.2x on FY26 core EPS. A three-turn de-rating is assumed as growth stays at the low end.

pillars.title: Growth has stalled at the low end
pillars.claim: Organic sales +1% for FY26 and flat in Q4; FY27 guide is 1% to 3%.

evidence.t: FY26 net sales $87.0B, +3%; organic +1%; Q4 organic flat

pillars.test: Does organic growth reach 2% in the first half of FY27?

pillars.title: Costs are the FY27 swing factor
pillars.claim: About $1B after tax of raw material, energy and transport costs is an 8% EPS drag; guide core EPS $6.89 to $7.11.
pillars.test: Does commodity inflation fade before the second half?

variant.ours: A great brand portfolio at a full price in a 5.2% rate world. The engine's stance rests on the multiple.
variant.could_be_wrong: A rotation into defensives would re-rate the multiple above 22x.

moat.summary: Brand portfolio with 50% gross margin and 22.7% operating margin; Walmart is about 16% of sales.

catalysts.label: P&G fiscal Q1 2027 earnings (date not confirmed; typically third or fourth week of October)

tripwires.text: Organic sales growth below 1% in a quarter

sources.title: Procter & Gamble Form 8-K, fiscal 2026 Q4 earnings release
